issues.description: The problem statement and the template define a public method named singFarmSong() in Farm that students must implement to play the song, but the solution implements a method named playFarmSong() instead. This name/signature mismatch between template/spec and solution can confuse students (they will look for singFarmSong() in the solution) and prevents a straightforward comparison between a student's implementation and the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution use the same method name/signature as the specification and template: rename playFarmSong() in the solution to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() method that delegates to the existing behavior. Alternatively, update the template/problem to reference playFarmSong() consistently if that name is preferred.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template define a Farm method named singFarmSong(), but the solution implementation provides the same functionality under the different name playFarmSong(). This diverging identifier for the same conceptual operation (playing/singing the farm song) creates mapping confusion for students reading the problem, working from the template, and comparing with the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or alternatively rename the template and problem references to playFarmSong(); the preferred fix is to rename playFarmSong() in the solution to singFarmSong() to match the problem statement and template.
